h5_latency.label: VM24_PRODUCTION_READ_ONLY
h5_latency.method: 7 serial samples per window, 0.3 s apart, one warm request discarded first
h5_latency.cache_assumption: warm: one discarded request per window before sampling
h5_latency.finding: delta-only is the SLOWEST despite returning fewer days than base-only (41 vs 51). Delta is t1/s256 geometry -- one chunk per day -- so a 41-day delta read touches ~41 chunks per variable, while base's (90,8,8) chunking serves 51 days from far fewer. This is §10.1's claim that cadence, not block size, governs the read cost of the delta tail, measured on production for the first time.

G3.reason: these are 1-concurrency point-range samples at one coordinate over 3 windows, not the 366-day p95 gate at its production percentile and load. They inform G3; they do not decide it.

H7_inode_headroom.reason: 225,490,340 free inodes against a +10y base projection of ~4.9M additional files -- roughly 46x headroom. Adjudication is the reviewer's, not this harness's.

H7_fd_rss.reason: 22 open fds and 78 MB RSS at rest. H7 asks for C=8/16 under sustained load, which was not run: it is not a read-only measurement.

G16.reason: metadata-scan and snapshot-open cost on the production tree were not measured; a full os.walk of a 5.4T store is not a low-rate read-only probe.
